title: Build a client-side router in TypeScript — 3 turns
description: Three turns build a client-side router: turn 1 addRoute/navigate, turn 2 params extraction, turn 3 nested routes.

task_spec.prompt: Implement `addRoute(pattern, handler)` in `src/router.ts` — push `{ pattern, handler }` to `this.routes`. Then implement `navigate(path)`: iterate routes, check if path exactly matches the pattern (for now ignore params), call the handler if matched, store in lastMatch, and return true. Return false if nothing matched. Run `npm test -- --forceExit`.
followup_prompts: Good. Now add `:param` extraction to `navigate()`. Convert the pattern to a regex by replacing `:paramName` segments with `([^/]+)` capture groups (escape slashes with anchors `^...$`). Extract param names from the pattern, then use the regex to extract values from the path. Build a params object and pass it to the handler. Run `npm test -- --forceExit` and fix any failures.
Final check: run `npm test -- --forceExit` one more time. All 6 tests must pass. The 'first matching route wins' test verifies that routes are checked in registration order.
success_criteria: Exact routes match and call handler
